title: Render re-derives document order via string position-tracking — the root of all 3 historical bug classes (the asymmetry's real cost)
evidence: tools/cnxml-render.js: 63 `.indexOf(` calls, 32 `extractNestedElements`, 15 `extractElements`, 21 `replace(...fullMatch,'')` strips, 38 `.match(`. The core engine (renderContent:696, renderTopLevelContent:924, renderExample:1354, renderExercise:1602, renderNote:1255) all follow the same strip-and-re-extract + `content.indexOf(fullMatch)` + `sort((a,b)=>a.position)` pattern. Position-tracking collides for ID-less elements: `content.indexOf('<para')` returns the FIRST `<para` at 4 sites (cnxml-render.js:829, 1092, 1293, 1437), so multiple ID-less paras get the same position. By contrast inject never does this — it consumes extraction's pre-ordered structure (buildElement dispatch at inject.js:1719) and only reaches for fragment DOM on the 3 hard containers (parseCnxmlFragment at inject.js:2280/2564/2824). The three named render bugs (figure-escapes-example, dropped <media> in notes, duplicate figures) are all ordering/containment failures of exactly this machinery.
description: The asymmetry isn't merely stylistic. Render reconstructs document order from scratch by scanning byte offsets, which is inherently ambiguous for repeated/ID-less elements and for nested containers (notes-inside-examples handled by manual `isInsideExample`/`isInsideExercise` offset-range checks at cnxml-render.js:784-795). Inject avoided this entire class because extraction already linearised the document. This is where the asymmetry hurts most and where future books (more nesting variety) will keep generating the same bug shape.
recommendation: Migrate render's STRUCTURE TRAVERSAL & ORDERING to DOM: walk `documentElement`/`<content>` childNodes in source order (order falls out for free, killing the position-collision class), serialize each block node back to a string with the existing serializeCnxmlFragment, and hand it to the unchanged leaf renderer. Do NOT rewrite leaf HTML emission in the same step.

title: Incremental DOM migration is VIABLE, not all-or-nothing — verified by round-trip probe across 3 books
evidence: Probe (DOMParser+XMLSerializer from @xmldom/xmldom 0.9, the same dep cnxml-dom.js uses) on real translated modules: efnafraedi-2e/03-translated/mt-preview/ch10/m68768.cnxml (69704 bytes, content children para+section), lifraen-efnafraedi/.../ch03/m00036.cnxml (figure+equation), edlisfraedi-2e/.../ch04/m42130.cnxml (section+para+note+exercise). All three: parsed=true, roundtrip=true, errs=0 — including `<m:math>` (MathML m: prefix) and numeric entities (`&#`). The seam already exists in cnxml-dom.js: parseCnxmlFragment (line 32), serializeCnxmlFragment (line 48, strips redundant xmlns), isBlockElement (line 115), BLOCK_TAGS (line 21).
description: The headline feasibility claim is empirically confirmed: a full translated module is well-formed XML that @xmldom/xmldom parses and round-trips losslessly across chemistry, organic, and physics. That means render can be migrated one element-type at a time behind a `serializeCnxmlFragment(node) -> existing renderX(string)` seam, with the DOM walk replacing only the traversal/ordering scaffolding. No flag day required.
recommendation: Adopt the leaf-seam pattern: a new DOM traversal (reusing cnxml-dom.js helpers) dispatches per node.localName to the EXISTING string renderers via serializeCnxmlFragment. Keep renderContent's regex path alive in parallel during migration; switch the dispatcher per element type as each is validated.

title: Reuse the in-repo migration precedent — but fix the oracle: render's gate is golden-HTML diff, NOT inject's compareTagCounts
evidence: The exact migration was already executed for inject: tools/__tests__/cnxml-dom-comparison.test.js runs old-regex vs new-DOM builders on real modules (TEST_MODULES with per-module `baseline` discrepancy budgets, lines 50-60) and asserts new <= baseline. But its oracle is `compareTagCounts` from cnxml-fidelity-check.js (import at comparison test line 23) — it compares CNXML tag counts on a round-trip, which is correct for inject (CNXML->CNXML) but wrong for render (CNXML->HTML). Render's existing tests (tools/__tests__/cnxml-render.test.js, 641 lines) are coarse `toContain` black-box assertions (e.g. line 157 `toContain('<p')`) — they will NOT catch ordering or escaping drift.
description: Mirror the proven parallel-run/zero-regression harness, but the comparison must be on rendered HTML. Snapshot current renderer output for all ~149 efnafraedi-2e modules (the mature book) as the golden baseline, then assert the DOM renderer is byte-identical (or diff-reviewed). renderCnxmlToHtml is already cleanly importable (exported at cnxml-render.js:4125; server consumes it via renderService.js:56 and pipeline routes), so capturing golden output is straightforward.
recommendation: Build a golden-HTML harness: render all efnafraedi-2e modules with the current renderer, store outputs, then run the DOM renderer and assert equality. Gate every phase on zero HTML diff against this baseline. This is the single most load-bearing 'keep tests green' detail and is easy to get wrong by analogy to inject's tag-count oracle.

title: Smallest high-value first phase: renderNote (the dropped-<media> bug site), then example, then exercise
evidence: inject piloted DOM on exactly example/exercise/note (buildExampleDom/buildExerciseDom/buildNoteDom, inject.js:2264/2554/2789), and the three historical render bugs live in these same containers. renderNote (cnxml-render.js:1255, ~100 lines) is the smallest and was the dropped-standalone-<media>-in-notes bug site. renderExample (1354) is the largest/most tangled (figure-in-para offset tracking at 1444-1451, the figure-escapes-example site). The fragment-DOM unit is proven: inject parses a single element's `match[0]` via parseCnxmlFragment (inject.js:2280) rather than the whole document — so the migration unit is per-container, low-blast-radius.
description: Phasing by risk/value: Phase 1 renderNote (S-M, smallest, proven bug site, validates the seam + golden-HTML harness). Phase 2 renderExample (M-L, highest historical bug density). Phase 3 renderExercise (M). Phase 4 (optional, L) migrate the top-level renderContent/renderTopLevelContent/renderSection ordering to a DOM childNodes walk — biggest structural payoff (kills the position-collision class) but touches every module, do it last once the seam is trusted. Leaf renderers (renderPara, renderTable, renderList, renderEquation, processInlineContent) need not change.
recommendation: Start with renderNote behind a parallel old-vs-new dispatcher gated by the golden-HTML harness from finding #3. Reuse parseCnxmlFragment/serializeCnxmlFragment/isBlockElement from cnxml-dom.js verbatim — they are renderer-agnostic. Ship each phase as its own PR with the harness green.

title: Scope correction: cnxml-dom.js is NOT a renderer — HTML emission must be ported separately, do not over-promise reuse
evidence: cnxml-dom.js (239 lines) emits zero HTML — it only parses/serializes/walks CNXML fragments (exports at line 229: parseCnxmlFragment, serializeCnxmlFragment, replaceParaContent, replaceListItems, removeElementsByTag, insertCnxmlBefore). All render HTML logic lives elsewhere: processInlineContent (tools/lib/cnxml-elements.js:668) for inline markers, mathjax-render.js for equations, resolveCrossModuleHref/buildCrossModuleHref (cnxml-elements.js:47/169) for links. These are string-in/string-out and are reused unchanged via the serialize seam — they are NOT replaced by cnxml-dom.js.
description: The accurate framing of 'reuse cnxml-dom.js': it supplies the structural traversal/ordering layer (replacing extractNestedElements + indexOf + fullMatch-strip), while the existing string leaf-renderers and processInlineContent stay behind the serialize seam. Conflating the two would imply rewriting all HTML emission — a much larger, riskier effort that is unnecessary and not what makes incremental work.
recommendation: In the migration plan, name two layers explicitly: (1) DOM traversal/ordering — new code reusing cnxml-dom.js; (2) HTML leaf emission — existing cnxml-elements.js/mathjax-render.js, untouched, invoked via serializeCnxmlFragment(node). Only layer 1 migrates per phase.

title: Content-gap renderers (os-embed, iframe) are a SEPARATE problem from string-vs-DOM — they, not the migration, block specific next books
evidence: cnxml-render.js has zero iframe handling (`grep -c iframe` = 0) — physics/biology PhET/YouTube `<iframe>` embeds render to nothing. os-embed is only partially handled (resolveOsEmbed at cnxml-render.js:137, used at 1704/1745) and organic chemistry routes ALL ~1961 exercises through `<link class="os-embed">`. The probe modules confirmed organic/physics translated CNXML parse fine — so the gap is missing RENDERERS, not malformed input. The system already ships 80% PERFECT (119/148 efnafraedi-2e modules) on the current string parser, so the string->DOM migration is an enabler, not a blocker.
description: Keep this distinct from the architecture migration so DOM isn't oversold: migrating to DOM does not render a single extra iframe or os-embed exercise — it only makes ADDING those renderers safer and ordering-correct. What actually blocks onboarding particular books is the absent content renderers: os-embed completeness blocks organic; iframe support blocks physics/biology.
recommendation: Track os-embed-exercise rendering (organic) and iframe/embed rendering (physics/biology) as their own findings/issues with their own acceptance tests, sequenced against which book is onboarded next. Ideally land them AFTER the relevant container is DOM-migrated so the new renderer is written once, on the DOM path.

title: Manifest reports false-green for un-injected books — `skippedUntranslated` hardcoded to 0, untranslated modules silently dropped
evidence: tools/lib/update-translation-errors.js:76 `if (!fs.existsSync(transPath)) continue;` drops every un-injected module without counting it; :108 writes `skippedUntranslated: 0` as a literal. Live manifests prove the lie: edlisfraedi-2e reports `totalChecked:9` of 283 source modules with `skipped:0`; liffraedi-2e `totalChecked:11` of 259 with `skipped:0`; orverufraedi `totalChecked:10`/159; lifraen-efnafraedi `totalChecked:8`/342. A book with zero injected modules produces `{perfect:0, withDiscrepancies:0, totalDiscrepancies:0}` and the CLI exits 0 (cnxml-fidelity-check.js:274 `process.exit(totalDiscrepancies>0?1:0)`).
description: The single most important answer to 'is this a reliable gate for scaling?': no. The manifest's denominator is invisible. At exactly the moment a new book is onboarded (few/no modules injected), the gate reads 'clean / exit 0'. The summary's `perfect` count is meaningless without the skipped count, and the skipped count is faked. For 4 of the 5 books today the manifest already covers under 5% of modules while advertising `skipped:0`.
recommendation: Increment a real counter on the `update-translation-errors.js:76` continue-branch and write it to `summary.skippedUntranslated`; also record `totalSourceModules`. Make exit-code/CI treat `skipped>0` as non-green (or at least non-perfect). Cheap: the discovery loop already walks all source modules, so the denominator is in hand.

title: The fidelity check is not actually a gate — never run in CI, inject never fails on a diff, render stage has no structural check at all
evidence: No CI invocation: grep of `.github/` and `package.json` for `fidelity`/`translation-errors` returns nothing. In inject, the only hard stop is *incomplete injection* (cnxml-inject.js:3385-3396 sets exitCode=1 + continue); the fidelity diff right after (3398-3410) is logged only when `args.verbose` and never affects exit code or whether the file is written. No server/editor code consumes the manifest or per-module reports (server grep clean except .venv noise). Crucially `compareTagCounts` is only ever run over inject output (03-translated CNXML); the inject→render→HTML stage — the ~4137-line string/regex parser (cnxml-render.js) where all three documented past bugs lived (figure-escapes-example, dropped <media> in notes, duplicate figures) — has no equivalent structural assertion.
description: translation-errors.json is an informational artifact committed by scripts/git-backup.sh, read by humans/AI, enforcing nothing. The asymmetry is the real risk: the safe DOM-based stage (inject, cnxml-dom.js) is the one that's checked; the fragile string-parsing stage (render) is the one that's unchecked. Scaling to 10-15 editors and 3-4 books with no automated structural gate means render regressions surface only by eyeball on namsbokasafn.is.
recommendation: Add a render-stage structural check that parses the produced HTML and asserts element/figure/note/example survival against the injected CNXML, then wire fidelity into CI as a non-blocking report (or blocking on regression vs the committed manifest). Reuse the existing real DOM in tools/lib/cnxml-dom.js rather than extending the string parser. This is the architectural change worth making now while chem is the only mature book.

title: Check is character-blind: untranslated English, mistranslation, dropped sentences, and corrupted math/text all pass as PERFECT
evidence: countTags (cnxml-fidelity-check.js:32-48) counts only opening element names via `/<([a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9:]*?)[\s>/]/g` (:42); text nodes and attribute values are never inspected. MathML is collapsed to `<m:math/>` (:35) so only the element count is compared, never its contents. This is why the null-byte incident (PR #167: Málstaður mangled `°`→`\x00` in 3 modules) was invisible to fidelity — character corruption preserves tag counts. A segment left 100% in English, a sentence dropped from a <para>, or a wrong-id `target-id` all yield zero diff.
description: Tag-count parity is necessary but nowhere near sufficient for a translation-fidelity gate. The discrepancy classes that matter most editorially for scaling (EN residue, semantic loss, equation corruption) are exactly the ones it cannot see. 'PERFECT fidelity' (cnxml-inject.js:3415) overstates what was verified.
recommendation: Don't bolt content-diffing onto the tag counter. Instead make fidelity feed the untranslated-EN-residue detector already planned in the editorial-throughput roadmap (Unit 4), and add a cheap C0/control-char scan of inject output (the `assertNoControlChars` guard already exists in api-translate.js — reuse it at the inject boundary too). Reframe the 'PERFECT' label to 'structure preserved' to stop overstating coverage.

title: CORRECTION: manifest is not truncated by partial re-injects; it is overwritten per-run/per-track, with a second uncontrolled producer
evidence: updateTranslationErrors (update-translation-errors.js:56-124) does a full-book on-disk rescan of `03-translated/<track>` every call and never reads/appends the prior manifest — so a same-track partial or failed re-inject (inject just `continue`s, leaving prior outputs on disk, cnxml-inject.js:3385-3396) does NOT shrink it. The real truncation is cross-track: track is resolved as `args.track || trackFromSourceDir(sourceDir)` (cnxml-inject.js:3279, 85-89), and `updateTranslationErrors` is called with that track (3425). Running inject `--track faithful` rewrites the whole manifest scanning only the faithful tree — efnafraedi-2e has 149 mt-preview outputs but only 4 faithful (`find ... | wc -l`), so the 149-module picture collapses to 4 and reports `perfect` against that. repair-emphasis.js is a second producer that also calls updateTranslationErrors, so the manifest's basis depends on whichever tool/track ran last.
description: The handed-down 'partial re-injects truncate it' claim is false for same-track operation. The actual failure mode is track confusion: as the project pivots from mt-preview to faithful (memory: only ~4 faithful modules exist), a faithful inject silently replaces a full mt-preview manifest with a near-empty faithful one — another false-green path, and one that will bite precisely during the faithful-content push.
recommendation: Make the manifest track-qualified (e.g. `translation-errors.<track>.json`, or store per-track sections in one file) so a faithful inject can't clobber the mt-preview record. Record the producing track + tool in the JSON header. Single source of the discovery loop (it's duplicated verbatim in cnxml-fidelity-check.js:79-99 and update-translation-errors.js:20-45 — factor out to avoid drift).

title: Attribute-blind and order-blind: bold↔italic swaps, link-kind changes, exercise variants, and mis-nested structure are all invisible
evidence: countTags keys only on element name (cnxml-fidelity-check.js:42), discarding attributes. So `<emphasis effect="italics">`↔`<emphasis effect="bold">` both count as `emphasis`; `<link url=...>` (external) vs `<link target-id=...>` (xref) vs `<link document=...>` (docref) all count as `link`; exercise/note `type=`/`class=` variants (flagged as a cross-book gap) collapse together. Counts are also position-independent: a `<figure>` moved into the wrong parent (the exact figure-escapes-example bug class) keeps total figure count equal and reports zero diff — only the duplicate-figure variant (count +1) would show.
description: Two whole discrepancy classes — attribute mutation and structural re-parenting/reordering — are outside the metric. These are not theoretical: the cross-book embed-kind variants and the past figure-nesting bugs fall squarely here. Editors trusting 'PERFECT' get no signal on emphasis-type drift or broken xref targets.
recommendation: For a meaningful structural gate, compare a normalized DOM shape (tag + key attributes like emphasis@effect, link target kind, exercise@class) rather than a flat name histogram — reuse @xmldom/xmldom already in tools/lib/cnxml-dom.js. At minimum, key emphasis counts by `effect` and link counts by which of url/target-id/document is present.

title: Tag-count signal-to-noise collapses on structurally-different books, making the metric unreadable as a gate at scale
evidence: Across only the handful of injected modules per book the diff density already diverges wildly: liffraedi-2e shows `totalDiscrepancies:326` over 11 modules (~30/module) vs efnafraedi-2e's 47 over 149 (~0.3/module); edlisfraedi-2e 78/9. Biology/physics carry structures chem lacks (iframe embeds, no <example>, deeper hierarchy per the cross-book findings), so even where the manifest IS populated, per-module diff counts in the tens drown any real regression signal.
description: A metric tuned to chem's near-perfect round-trip produces hundreds of diffs on biology before any editor touches it, so 'discrepancy count went up' carries no actionable meaning for the new books. The number can't function as a pass/fail or even a trend gate without per-book baselining.
recommendation: Baseline per book: store an accepted-discrepancy snapshot per module and gate on *delta vs baseline* (new/regressed tags), not absolute count. Classify known-benign tags (e.g. the sub/sup/term overcounting from EN-marker conversion already documented) so they don't inflate every book's totals.

title: Emphasis-collapse normalization deliberately masks a known API loss class (low) and 148 stale per-module `-fidelity.json` artifacts have no consumer
evidence: cnxml-fidelity-check.js:36-40 collapses `<emphasis X><emphasis X>`→single in BOTH source and translated before counting, so genuine same-type nested-emphasis flattening (a documented API gap) is hidden by design ('Renders identically'). Separately, `--report` writes per-module `<module>-fidelity.json` next to the CNXML (writeReport :116-133) — 148 of these are committed under books/efnafraedi-2e/03-translated/mt-preview/ (`find ... -name '*-fidelity.json' | wc -l` = 148) — a parallel artifact with a richer schema (timestamp, direction) than the book-level manifest, written by a different code path, read by nothing.
description: The emphasis masking is an intentional renders-identically simplification (acceptable), but it means the metric cannot report a real markup-loss class, and 18 emphasis diffs remain the top noise category anyway. The per-module reports are a divergent, stale second representation that will confuse maintainers about which file is authoritative as more books/editors arrive.
recommendation: Document the emphasis-collapse as a deliberate exclusion in the file header so it isn't mistaken for a bug. Either delete the committed `-fidelity.json` artifacts and the `--report`/`--annotate` paths, or fold their richer schema into the single book-level manifest so there's one source of truth.

title: Two divergent parseSegments implementations + 4–5 distinct SEG-marker regexes across the pipeline
evidence: Same marker, different parsers: tools/cnxml-inject.js:168 `/<!-- SEG:([^\s]+) -->[ \t]*\n?([\s\S]*?)(?=<!-- SEG:|$)/g` → returns a Map, first-match-wins, HTML-comment ONLY. server/services/segmentParser.js:24 `/(?:<!--\s*SEG:([\w]+):([\w-]+):([\w-]+)\s*-->|\{\{SEG:...\}\})/` → returns an Array, structured 3-group, ALSO accepts mustache `{{SEG:}}`. api-translate.js:143/158 repair with `/<!-- SEG:(\S+?) -->/g`; api-translate.js:275/294 normalize with `<!--\s*SEG:`. cnxml-extract.js:1583 emits `<!-- SEG:${seg.id} -->`. The marker-vs-line-based parser bug (CLAUDE.md #96; segmentParser.js:104-112 comment) is direct evidence these two parsers already silently diverged once and dropped whole modules.
description: Segment parsing is reimplemented at least twice with incompatible contracts (return type, dedup policy, marker dialects, whitespace tolerance). They agree only by luck on today's canonical files; any drift re-creates the #96 class of bug where the editor and inject disagree about how many segments a file has. This is exactly the architecture-asymmetry pattern flagged project-wide, localized to segment handling, and it gets riskier as 3-4 books and 10-15 editors arrive.
recommendation: Extract one shared `tools/lib/seg-markers.js` (CommonJS+ESM interop already exists in tools/lib) exposing a single canonical regex, a `tokenize(content) -> [{segmentId,moduleId,type,elementId,raw}]`, and an explicit documented duplicate policy. Have cnxml-extract, api-translate, cnxml-inject, and server/services/segmentParser all consume it. Do this now while efnafraedi-2e is the only mature book and divergence is cheap to fix.

title: Duplicate segment IDs handled three different ways (inject first-wins, editor last-wins, count counts-all)
evidence: 83 of 170 canonical efnafraedi-2e EN files contain duplicate SEG ids (0 in edlisfraedi-2e/liffraedi-2e/lifraen-efnafraedi/orverufraedi). Handling diverges: inject keeps the FIRST (cnxml-inject.js:175 `if (segments.has(id)) duplicateCount++; else segments.set(id,text)`), the editor keeps the LAST (segmentParser.js:231 `isLookup[seg.segmentId] = seg` overwrite), and countModuleSegments counts ALL markers (segmentParser.js:543 `return matches ? matches.length : 0`). The inject docstring itself (cnxml-inject.js:160-162) warns duplicates can carry DIFFERENT content (MATH numbering). applyApprovedEdits rebuilds via `data.segments.map` (segmentEditorService.js:731) so both duplicate rows are re-emitted.
description: When duplicate occurrences differ, the editor displays/edits a different occurrence than inject ships, and the dashboard denominator (countModuleSegments) is inflated versus inject's deduped set, so progress percentages and 'translatedCount' (segmentParser.js:278) overcount. The fact that this 'works' today depends on duplicates happening to be identical — accidental, not designed.
recommendation: Pick one policy (first-wins, to match inject) and apply it in the shared lib from finding #1; have loadModuleForEditing build isLookup with `if(!isLookup[id])` and surface a per-module duplicate count to the dashboard. Better: dedupe at extraction so duplicate SEG ids never reach the segment files.

title: --allow-en-fallback is a per-run, whole-chapter switch — silently ships English for EVERY untranslated module in the chapter
evidence: findChapterModules returns ALL modules when --module is omitted (cnxml-inject.js:3154-3155), the default. main() loops every module and passes the single `args.allowEnFallback` into each loadModuleInputs call (cnxml-inject.js:3303). loadModuleInputs only opts into EN per file-existence (cnxml-inject.js:3180-3198): if the faithful/mt file is absent and the flag is set, it loads `02-for-mt/.../-segments.en.md` and warns to stderr only.
description: With partially-translated chapters (the normal state once many editors are mid-Pass-1), a single `--allow-en-fallback` on a chapter-wide inject publishes raw English for every module that isn't done yet — not the one module the operator meant to force. The only signal is a stderr warning buried among per-module output. This scales badly to 10-15 editors working a chapter concurrently.
recommendation: Restrict EN fallback to runs that pass an explicit `--module`, or require a per-module opt-in list, and emit a machine-readable manifest (e.g. into translation-errors.json) of exactly which modules fell back to English so the publish step can refuse or flag them.

title: Injection gate checks segment PRESENCE, never translatedness — untranslated-English residue passes as COMPLETE
evidence: The only safety checks are: file existence (cnxml-inject.js:3180), per-segment presence where empty string is treated as missing (getSeg cnxml-inject.js:1481 `if (!text)`), and `report.complete = stats.segmentsMissing.length===0 && stats.mathUnresolved.length===0` (cnxml-inject.js:1677). A segment present with still-English text (API echo of proper nouns/formulas, or MT passthrough) is returned verbatim by getSeg (1488-1496) and reported COMPLETE. Title fallbacks substitute the English structure.json text outright: `getSeg(...) || element.title.text` at cnxml-inject.js:1512, 1756, 1795, 2185, 2337 (these do still mark the seg missing, so they fail safe, but illustrate EN leaking into output paths). The throughput roadmap names an 'untranslated-EN-residue detector' as not-yet-built (CLAUDE.md Unit 4).
description: There is no per-segment 'is this actually Icelandic?' check anywhere in the segment path. As more books onboard (more formula-heavy/proper-noun-heavy content) and more MT volume flows, English segments will ship silently with a green COMPLETE status — the opposite of the human-verified-asset guarantee Pass 1 is supposed to provide.
recommendation: Add an EN≈IS residue check (flag segments whose IS content equals the EN source after stripping markers/numbers/symbols, above a min token threshold) in the shared lib, surfaced both at inject (downgrade report.complete or list residues) and at save/submit in segmentEditorService. Reuse the existing getSegmentQaFindings hook (segmentEditorService.js:203) rather than a new path.

title: SEG-marker whitespace mismatch: inject/split require a literal single space, editor/normalize accept any whitespace
evidence: inject parseSegments matches literal `<!-- SEG:` with one space (cnxml-inject.js:168) and splitAtSegBoundaries lookahead is `(?=<!-- SEG:)` literal (api-translate.js:438), while the editor regex is `<!--\s*SEG:` (segmentParser.js:24) and normalizeSegMarkers uses `<!--\s*SEG:` (api-translate.js:275,294). All 294,836 live markers use exactly one space (verified), so this is latent.
description: A marker emitted with zero or two spaces after `<!--` would parse in the editor but be invisible to inject (folded into the previous segment's text). It fails safe today (the lost id becomes a missing segment → report incomplete → blocked) but is a confusing footgun for any future producer or hand-edit, and a likely source of the next #96-style 'render not found' misdiagnosis.
recommendation: Use the single tolerant regex from finding #1 everywhere (`<!--\s*SEG:...\s*-->`), eliminating the literal-space variants in inject and splitAtSegBoundaries.

title: 67 orphan `*-segments(b|c|d).en.md` files carry legacy mustache {{SEG:}} markers half the pipeline can't parse
evidence: `find books -name '*-segments(*.md'` → 67 files; all `{{SEG:}}` markers in the tree live in these variant files (grep for `{{SEG:}}` matched only `m*-segments(b).en.md` etc., 0 canonical files). They don't match the `${moduleId}-segments.${lang}.md` path inject/editor construct, so they are never loaded — but inject's parseSegments couldn't read their mustache format anyway (cnxml-inject.js:168 is HTML-comment-only), while segmentParser.js:24 can.
description: Dead, format-inconsistent artifacts in the content tree. Harmless today but they (a) pollute any future glob that scans 02-for-mt, (b) demonstrate the mustache dialect is real input the editor accepts yet inject silently can't, and (c) will confuse new editors onboarding the workflow.
recommendation: Delete or move the `*-segments(b|c|d).*.md` variants out of 02-for-mt (confirm with the user first — they are under a generated dir, not 01-source). Drop mustache `{{SEG:}}` support from segmentParser entirely once confirmed unused, so the editor and inject accept the same dialect.

title: Highest-risk construct: os-embed external exercises render complete-looking English that passes review silently
evidence: books/lifraen-efnafraedi/01-source: 1959 of 1961 <exercise> bodies are a bare <link class="os-embed" url="#exercise/..."/> with NO translatable text (e.g. ch11/m00128.cnxml prob-00001). The exercise content lives in external English JSON: books/lifraen-efnafraedi/01-source/exercises/*.json (1961 files, one per nickname). Sample 01-03-OC-P01.json: stimulus_html="What is the ground-state electron configuration of each of the following elements:", questions[0].stem_html="Oxygen" — English. These JSONs are consumed ONLY by cnxml-render.js resolveOsEmbed() (tools/cnxml-render.js:137-157, called at 1704-1745); grep shows no other tool/server file references stem_html/stimulus_html/01-source/exercises. cnxml-extract.js has zero os-embed handling, so the exercise text never enters extract→MT→inject. By contrast efnafraedi/edlisfraedi/liffraedi/orverufraedi all have os-embed=0.
description: The pipeline structurally cannot translate os-embed exercises: the CNXML carries no text, and the external JSON is never fed to MT. cnxml-render.js silently fills the gap from the English cache, so organic chemistry's entire exercise corpus renders as fluent, complete-looking English. This is worse than a visible drop (cf. iframe) because nothing looks broken — a linguistic reviewer sees a finished page and the missing translation never surfaces. The os-embed RESOLVER already works; the only gap is that stem_html/stimulus_html bypass extract→MT→inject. This is organic-only among the 5 onboarded books, so it is a risk for a NEW title ONLY IF that title exhibits the construct (not verifiable from this repo — only organic's source is present).
recommendation: Add an os-embed extraction path that reuses the existing pipeline: have cnxml-extract.js emit segments from each cached exercise JSON's stimulus_html + stem_html + solutions, run them through MT/review like any segment, and have resolveOsEmbed() prefer a translated sidecar (e.g. exercises/<nickname>.is.json) over the English original. Until then, treat any os-embed-bearing book as exercise-untranslated and surface a per-module warning in render so the gap is visible, not silent.

title: No pre-intake structural gate exists — a candidate title's fitness cannot be assessed before sinking intake effort
evidence: The only structural-profile artifact, docs/openstax-expansion-feasibility-study.md (2026-02-11), is prospective prose, not a runnable check; it predates the actual onboarding of physics/biology/organic/microbiology and never mentions organic or microbiology at all. No script in tools/ scans a candidate's CNXML for the constructs proven to break (os-embed, iframe, glossary-absence, missing BOOK_CONFIGS entry). getBookRenderConfig (tools/lib/book-rendering-config.js:350-363) only warns to console for unknown books.
description: Because the next 3-4 titles' source is not in this repo (only the 5 onboarded books plus an empty stjornufraedi/ shell), there is currently no way to tell whether a candidate is safe to onboard until intake is half-done and rendering reveals the gaps. This meta-gap is the one item that genuinely blocks confident onboarding of the next book.
recommendation: Add a one-shot pre-intake probe (small script or checklist) run against any candidate's raw CNXML before committing intake. Minimum checks, each tied to a proven failure: (1) grep 'class="os-embed"' >0 → no translation path (finding 1); (2) grep '<iframe' >0 → silently dropped in extract AND render (finding 3); (3) <glossary> count==0 while <term> present → compiled Lykilhugtök page renders empty (finding 4); (4) no BOOK_CONFIGS entry yet → silent default-degrade (finding 5); plus element counts for the difference matrix (finding 6). Gate intake on a clean/triaged probe.

title: <iframe> interactive embeds are silently dropped in both extract and render
evidence: Source counts: edlisfraedi-2e (physics) 57 <iframe>, liffraedi-2e (biology) 51 <iframe> (PhET sims / YouTube, per study §4.2/§5.3). grep 'iframe' returns ZERO hits in tools/cnxml-extract.js and zero emitting hits in tools/cnxml-render.js (only os-embed doc comments). Confirms the seeded finding. Both affected books are already onboarded, so this is live content loss, not a future risk.
description: Any <iframe> inside <media>/<note class="interactive"> disappears from rendered output. Physics and biology already lose ~108 interactive elements between them; future interactive titles would too. Visible-ish (a note renders empty) but easy to miss at scale.
recommendation: Add an iframe branch to render (emit a responsive <iframe> or a captioned external-resource link with translated surrounding note text) and ensure extract preserves the embed + its alt/caption as a non-translatable marker. Cross-repo flag: the rendered iframe styling lives in namsbokasafn-vefur static/styles/content.css — coordinate, do not edit here.

title: Books without <glossary> render an empty compiled "Lykilhugtök" page
evidence: <glossary> element counts: efnafraedi-2e 109, edlisfraedi-2e 229, liffraedi-2e 205, lifraen-efnafraedi 0, orverufraedi 0. Organic instead uses <section class="key-terms"> (31); microbiology has 0 of either despite 6395 inline <term>. Render's glossary path keys strictly off the <glossary> element: tools/cnxml-render.js:873 (/<glossary>([\s\S]*?)<\/glossary>/) and the compiled EOC glossary page at :2263. SHARED_END_OF_CHAPTER.glossary (book-rendering-config.js:36-42, compiled:true) is inherited by ALL books including organic/microbiology.
description: For organic and microbiology the compiled 'Lykilhugtök' (Key Terms) page has no source the renderer recognizes, so it renders empty even though terminology exists (key-terms sections / inline <term>). This is exactly the study's Precalculus 'inline <term> only, no formal glossary' warning (§6.3) — already a live reality in two onboarded books, and a near-certainty for math/newer titles next.
recommendation: Add an alternative glossary extractor that builds the compiled page from <section class="key-terms"> (organic) and/or inline <term> definitions (microbiology), selected per-book in book-rendering-config.js. Add the '<glossary>==0 with <term> present' check to the pre-intake probe (finding 2).

title: Unknown-book rendering silently degrades instead of failing loud
evidence: getBookRenderConfig (tools/lib/book-rendering-config.js:350-363) returns a fallback config with only console.warn for any slug not in BOOK_CONFIGS (the 5 registered books at :335-341). Fallback gives English-derived note labels via generateFallbackLabel (:372-380) and a single 'summary' end-of-chapter section, so exercise sections and notes mis-render.
description: Onboarding a 6th title without first adding a BOOK_CONFIGS entry produces a page that renders without error but with wrong/English note labels and missing exercise pages — a quiet quality failure that a console warning in a CLI run is easy to miss.
recommendation: Make book registration an explicit gate: either throw on unknown slug in the render/inject entrypoints (require an opt-in --allow-default flag), or have the pre-intake probe assert a BOOK_CONFIGS entry exists. Every new title MUST add a config object (note labels, endOfChapterSections, excludedSectionClasses) — document this as step 1 of intake.

title: Empirical difference matrix (re-counted) — corrects seeded/study numbers; confirms MathML passthrough is NOT a blocker
evidence: Re-counted across 01-source (modules; equation; example; glossary; exercise; note; m:math; iframe; os-embed; footnote; term): efnafraedi-2e 149;1559;301;109;1736;460;5369;0;0;36;1615 | edlisfraedi-2e 283;2396;289;229;3867;428;18478;57;0;42;1919 | liffraedi-2e 259;41;0;205;1509;461;85;51;0;42;4799 | lifraen-efnafraedi 342;56;102;0;1961;4;416;0;1959;0;554 | orverufraedi 159;35;0;0;1166;711;61;0;0;458;6395. CORRECTIONS: microbiology footnotes = 458 (seed said 355); biology <example>=0 confirmed; microbiology <example>=0 confirmed; organic os-embed 1959 (seed ~1961 = total exercises, 1959 are os-embed). Distinct note classes: chemistry 4, physics 1 (+title-only), biology ~9, microbiology 7 (confirmed). Study module estimates were high (biology 280→259, physics 318→283).
description: Physics already carries 18478 <m:math> blocks and renders via opaque passthrough without issue, confirming the study's 'MathML density = Low pipeline impact' assessment — MathML volume is reassurance, not a blocker, for the next (likely math-heavy) title. The study's Phase-1 'parameterize + per-book config' work is effectively DONE: tools/lib/book-rendering-config.js is a 5-book registry with note labels, EOC sections, exercise-class resolution and a fallback; tools take --book. The study should be retired/rewritten as this empirical per-book profile.
recommendation: Replace docs/openstax-expansion-feasibility-study.md's prospective tables with this measured matrix and mark Phase-1 parameterization complete. Keep the matrix as the baseline the pre-intake probe (finding 2) appends each new candidate to.

title: validateMarkers is a count-only check — blind to inline [[bracket]] marker loss AND intra-segment truncation
evidence: tools/api-translate.js:255-259 counts only `<!-- SEG:` and compares input==output. grep confirms NO `[[` handling anywhere in api-translate.js or malstadur-api.js (0 hits). Inline markers ([[i:]], [[xref:]], [[link:]], and the lossy [[BR]]/[[MEDIA]] at ~2-3% loss per context) are never validated at the MT boundary. Same blind spot covers intra-segment truncation: a chunk with 1 segment has 1 SEG marker in / 1 out even if the segment body is truncated mid-text, so validateMarkers passes (currently latent — largest single segment measured is only 2451 chars vs 25000 chunk limit, 10x headroom, but async truncates ~33-35KB).
description: The only structural integrity gate at the producer boundary counts top-level segment markers. Inline bracket-marker loss (the documented [[BR]]/[[MEDIA]] ~2-3% drop) flows silently through MT → inject → render and only surfaces as missing line-breaks/images in published HTML, three stages downstream. As physics/biology onboard (iframe/PhET/YouTube → [[MEDIA]]-class markers, higher inline-marker density), this silent-loss surface grows. This is the same class of defect the file already guards against elsewhere (assertNoControlChars, countInlineMarkers) — catching corruption at the MT producer boundary.
recommendation: Add a producer-boundary check that counts bracket markers BY TYPE (content is translated, so only the count+type per marker family is comparable) and warns/fails on a per-type input≠output mismatch, mirroring the existing assertNoControlChars/countInlineMarkers philosophy. Reuse the marker regexes already used by cnxml-inject. Keep it advisory-with-summary like normalizeSegMarkers so clean output is a no-op. This is a natural low-friction add, not a new pattern.

title: pollTask's poll GET is not wrapped in withRetry — one transient blip fails the whole module on the dominant production path
evidence: malstadur-api.js:293 `const task = await apiRequest(apiKey, 'GET', `/v1/translate/tasks/${taskId}`);` is a BARE call inside the poll loop (up to 180 polls / 6 min, lines 291-314). Contrast translate() at :233 and translateAsync() at :266, both wrapped in withRetry. Any single transient 5xx/network error on any poll throws straight out. This path is dominant: 116/149 chem modules exceed SYNC_CHAR_LIMIT (10K) so translateAuto (:330-336) routes them through translateAsync+pollTask; only ~33 use the sync path. grep confirms the entire client (createClient/translateAuto/translateAsync/pollTask/withRetry) has ZERO test coverage (NONE in tools/__tests__).
description: The submit step retries but the polling steps do not, so the most-used translation path is the least resilient: a 6-minute polling window with no transient-error tolerance on any individual poll. A momentary network hiccup mid-poll aborts a module that the API may have translated successfully. The total absence of tests for the async/retry machinery means this went unnoticed.
recommendation: Wrap the line-293 poll GET in the existing withRetry helper (same pattern as :233/:266). Add focused tests for the async path (translateAuto routing at the 10K boundary, pollTask completed/failed/timeout, withRetry 5xx-vs-4xx behavior) using a mocked fetch. Reliability fix, not a content-corruption risk — a failed module fails loud and is re-run.

title: Glossary filtering matches by raw substring with no word boundaries and lossy case-folding
evidence: tools/api-translate.js:413-419 `lowerText.includes(t.sourceWord.toLowerCase())`. Of 617 approved chem terms, 6 are ≤3 chars (gas, ion, pH, ray, STP, ΔH°). Measured raw substring hits in a sample sentence: 'ph' (from pH lowercased) matched 6 times (phase, phosphorus, graph, morphology, …), 'ion' 3 times (ionization, region, …), 'ray' 1 (X-ray). So short/case-sensitive terms like pH get force-included against unrelated words and lose their casing in the match.
description: filterGlossaryForText over-includes glossary terms whenever a short source word appears as a substring of unrelated words. If the API applies glossaries by token this risks mis-mapping; if it applies them token-level it is merely payload bloat and noise. Either way word-boundary matching removes the ambiguity cheaply. Lowercasing pH→ph also defeats case-sensitive chemical notation.
recommendation: Match on word boundaries (e.g. a per-term regex with \b … \b, or token-set intersection) instead of String.includes, and avoid case-folding case-significant terms. Low cost, removes the ambiguity regardless of how the API consumes glossaries.

title: Control-char (NUL/degree-sign) failure aborts the whole module with no retry, unlike the truncation path which retries
evidence: tools/api-translate.js:478 assertNoControlChars throws immediately (fail-loud, by design, PR #167). The adjacent truncation case at :483-504 instead retries once (without glossary) before throwing. The °→NUL mangling is a known intermittent Málstaður bug.
description: The two known intermittent API corruptions are handled asymmetrically: truncation gets one automatic retry, a NUL byte gets none — one mangled degree sign fails the entire module and requires manual re-run. Fail-loud-terminal is the deliberate PR #167 control to stop silent corruption, so this is an optional enhancement, not a defect.
recommendation: Optionally mirror the existing truncation-retry: on a control-char detection, retry the chunk once, and only fail loud if the retry is also dirty (preserving fail-loud as the terminal state). Open question that decides whether it helps: is the °→NUL mangling deterministic for identical input (retry wastes a call) or transient (retry recovers)? Cannot be determined from the client; decide before implementing.

title: 429 retry uses fixed exponential backoff — ignores Retry-After and has no jitter
evidence: malstadur-api.js:87-100: 429 is retryable but withRetry computes `initialBackoff * Math.pow(2, attempt)` (1s,2s,4s; MAX_RETRIES=3) with no read of the response's Retry-After header and no jitter. MalstadurApiError captures statusCode/body (:109-116) but the header is discarded in apiRequest (:120-151).
description: Defensive-hardening only — there is no evidence of actual Málstaður 429s in production (the 429s in project memory are the editorial server's OWN E2E rate limiter, unrelated). If whole-book runs (149+ sequential modules) ever hit server-side throttling, fixed backoff without honoring Retry-After is a weaker control than the API may be signalling.
recommendation: When a 429 carries Retry-After, honor it; otherwise add jitter to the exponential backoff. Capture the header in MalstadurApiError.body or a dedicated field. Low priority pending any real evidence of Málstaður throttling.

title: Cost-estimate magic number duplicated; dry-run estimates from raw input chars, not billable units
evidence: The `* 5 / 1000` (5 ISK/1000 chars) constant appears in two files: malstadur-api.js:52 (estimatedISK, from API-reported usage.units) and api-translate.js:742 (dry-run, from raw fs input char count). The dry-run sums `content.length` (:733-742) while actual billing uses the API's `usage.units` (:38-42), which can diverge with glossary/markup overhead.
description: Minor housekeeping. The rate constant is unsynchronized across two files (a price change must be edited in both), and the dry-run cost can mislead because it counts source characters rather than the units the API actually bills.
recommendation: Extract the ISK-per-1000-chars rate to a single exported constant in malstadur-api.js and reuse it in the dry-run. Optionally label the dry-run estimate as 'source chars (pre-billing)' to set expectations.

title: Design check: clean-cut SEG splitting is correct (overlapping-split not warranted) and chunking is appropriately lean (not over-engineered)
evidence: splitAtSegBoundaries (tools/api-translate.js:437-460) never splits mid-segment; per-chunk glossary is re-filtered in translateChunk (:469). DEFAULT_MAX_CHUNK_CHARS=25000 (:428) vs the documented ~33-35KB async truncation point, with the margin justified by glossary payload headroom (filtered glossary typically 2-5KB).
description: Addressing the two explicit asks. (1) Overlapping-split would NOT improve this client: SEG segments are independent translation units, cross-chunk context loss is at most one boundary per 25K, and the glossary (not chunk adjacency) carries term consistency — overlapping would add API cost and dedup complexity for negligible quality gain. Clean-cut is the right choice. (2) Over-engineering is minimal: the only conservative edge is that modules in the 25-33KB band get split into 2 calls where 1 might fit, but that is justified by glossary headroom against the truncation point. The chunking/limit logic is lean and appropriate.
recommendation: No change to splitting strategy. If call-count optimization is ever desired, the 25K limit could be made glossary-size-aware (raise toward ~30K when the filtered glossary is small) — but this is not worth the added branching today.

title: List-flattening remediation diverges: examples PRESERVE the nested list, exercises and notes DELETE it
evidence: All three DOM builders detect the same condition (para segment text contains expanded math AND a sibling <list> is a DOM descendant of the para, i.e. extraction flattened the list into the para text): buildExampleDom tools/cnxml-inject.js:2352-2366. But the remediation is INVERTED. buildExampleDom:2354-2376 sets skipParaText=true, KEEPS the <list> element, empties the para text, then calls replaceListItemsDom -> structured <list><item> survives. buildExerciseDom:2597-2607 and buildNoteDom:2854-2863 instead call `siblingEl.parentNode.removeChild(siblingEl)` -> the <list> is DELETED and the full flattened paraText is injected as inline text. The code comments at 2595 and 2853 ('same embedded-list detection as buildExampleDom') mask the divergence: the detection is identical, the action is opposite. books/efnafraedi-2e/translation-errors.json shows para-count drift in 2 modules (para diff -7, -1), consistent with paras being collapsed; checker does not tag by container so it cannot localize this.
description: For the identical input pattern (a para whose extracted segment text absorbed a nested list), an example renders a real Icelandic bulleted/numbered list while an exercise or note renders the same content as one flat run of inline text with the <list>/<item> semantics destroyed. The example path is the correct one (it de-duplicates by emptying para text and re-injecting structured items); the exercise/note paths are lossy of list structure. This is a genuine correctness inconsistency in the mature chemistry book today, and it will diverge more as exercise/note-heavy books (microbiology, biology) onboard.
recommendation: Unify buildExerciseDom and buildNoteDom onto buildExampleDom's approach: when the flattened-list condition holds, set skipParaText (inject only the title/empty), KEEP the <list> element, and let replaceListItemsDom translate the items. Factor the shared para+list handling out of the three *Dom builders into one helper in tools/lib/cnxml-dom.js so the remediation cannot drift again. Better still, have cnxml-extract.js mark a flattened list explicitly in structure rather than have three builders sniff for '<m:math' (see separate finding).

title: Tables are the only complex element never moved to DOM; cell replacement is self-described "simplified" positional regex
evidence: buildTable tools/cnxml-inject.js:1913-1982 extracts the original <table> by regex and replaces <row>/<entry> content positionally with nested String.replace callbacks; line 1933 comment: 'This is simplified - a full implementation would need to match entries by position'. It is the one complex construct still on the string path while buildExampleDom/buildExerciseDom/buildNoteDom use @xmldom DOM (tools/lib/cnxml-dom.js). All five books are table-heavy and use spanning cells (source counts: efnafraedi-2e 191 tables / 183 morerows|namest; orverufraedi 117 / 234; lifraen-efnafraedi 88 / 128; edlisfraedi-2e 103 / 98; liffraedi-2e 64 / 86). The prior three production rebuild bugs (figure-escapes-example, dropped media in notes, duplicate figures) were all string-parsing bugs of exactly this shape.
description: Positional cell matching (rowIdx/cellIdx) assumes structure.rows[].cells[] aligns 1:1 with the regex-walked <entry> elements. Spanning cells (morerows makes later rows carry fewer <entry> elements; namest/nameend column spans) are precisely where positional alignment drifts, mis-assigning or duplicating translated cell text. I confirmed the capability gap (string-only, by-position, no span awareness) but did NOT observe a concrete misalignment instance, since that also depends on whether extraction's rows[].cells[] already compensates for spans -- unverified. Treat as a high-likelihood latent gap, not a counted incidence.
recommendation: Port buildTable to the DOM path used by the other complex builders: parseCnxmlFragment(originalTable), walk <row>/<entry> nodes, replace content via replaceParaContentDom / a cell analog, serialize via serializeCnxmlFragment. The self-closing <entry/> normalization at 1460/1930 becomes unnecessary under a real parser. Before doing so, add a focused fixture with morerows + namest to confirm extraction's cell model, since the DOM rewrite must consume whatever structure.rows[].cells[] provides.

title: All media-rebuild paths emit only <image>; <iframe> (PhET/YouTube) is lost unless it rides inside an original-preserved container
evidence: Three rebuild paths hardcode a single <image> child and cannot represent <iframe>/<flash>/audio/video: buildMediaElement (inline [[MEDIA:N]] restore) tools/cnxml-inject.js:1030-1038; buildMedia (block 'media' element) :2986-3001; buildFigure fallback :1881-1896. The root cause is upstream: extraction's inline-media capture only reads <image> attrs and stores src='' when there is no image -- tools/cnxml-extract.js:188-197. Concrete inject-side loss instance: books/edlisfraedi-2e/01-source/ch??/m42185.cnxml has `<media id="concept-trailer-buoyancy"><iframe src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/..."/>` inline in a <para> (no <image>); extraction turns it into [[MEDIA:N]] with empty src, and buildMediaElement re-emits `<media><image src=""/></media>` -- the video is replaced by a broken empty image. Context classification: edlisfraedi-2e has 57 iframes (40 inside <note>, which survive because buildNoteDom serializes the original DOM; 17 inline-in-para/top-level, which hit the image-only rebuild and are lost). liffraedi-2e has 51 iframes, ALL inside <note> -- so biology loses none at inject (its loss is render-side, Pillar 1).
description: iframe survival at the rebuild stage is accidental: it works only when the iframe happens to live inside a note/example/exercise whose fragment is preserved by DOM serialization. Any iframe inline in a para (->[[MEDIA]]) or as a standalone block media (->buildMedia) is silently degraded to an empty image. This blocks faithful onboarding of physics specifically (17 confirmed instances); biology is unaffected at inject.
recommendation: Capture the full inner XML of a <media> in extraction (not just image src/mime), and on rebuild preserve non-image media verbatim: in buildMediaElement/buildMedia, if the captured media has no <image> (or has an <iframe>/other child), re-emit the stored original media markup rather than synthesizing an <image>. Coordinate with namsbokasafn-vefur (CSS/render contract) on how iframes are presented downstream -- FLAG cross-repo, do not edit there.

title: Every DOM builder bootstraps from a lazy greedy regex extraction against the raw module string
evidence: buildExampleDom:2270, buildExerciseDom:2557, buildNoteDom:2817, buildFigure:1829, buildTable:1917, buildEquation:2921 all locate their element with `new RegExp('<tag\\s+id="ID"[^>]*>[\\s\\S]*?</tag>')` against originalCnxml, then (for the *Dom ones) parseCnxmlFragment on the captured slice. The lazy `[\s\S]*?` stops at the FIRST closing tag, so any same-tag nesting (note-in-note, example-in-example, table-in-entry) captures a truncated fragment. Verified safe TODAY: note-in-note = 0 across all five books. So this is latent, not active.
description: The 'DOM rebuild' path is really 'regex-extract a slice, then DOM-parse the slice'. It re-introduces string parsing at the entry point of the very path that exists to avoid string parsing, and its correctness rests on an invariant (no same-tag nesting) that holds for the current five books but is not enforced and not guaranteed for the 3-4 books being onboarded. It also forces awkward whole-document regex side-channels (e.g. the note-inside-example position check in buildNoteDom:2795-2814).
recommendation: Parse the whole module CNXML into one DOM once at the top of buildCnxml, pass the document down, and locate elements via doc.getElementById(element.id) instead of per-element regex extraction. This removes ~6 fragile regexes, makes the note-nesting check a DOM ancestor walk, and is the structural change worth making now while chemistry is the only mature book.

title: buildExerciseDom drops id-less exercises entirely; buildGenericElement recurses without ctx
evidence: Two distinct robustness bugs on the id-less fallback path. (a) buildExerciseDom:2555 `if (!element.id) return null` discards the whole exercise, whereas buildExampleDom:2266 and buildNoteDom:2791 fall back to buildGenericElement -- inconsistent, and the exercise variant is outright content loss. (b) buildGenericElement signature (:3006) takes no ctx and its child recursion (:3023) calls `buildElement(child, getSeg, equations, originalCnxml)` with ctx omitted, so figure de-dup tracking (figuresHandledInContainers/Notes), imageMapping (translated-SVG basename swaps), and inlineTables are all lost for any child built under the generic path. Reachability today: id-less <exercise>/<example>/<note> = 0 across all five books, so neither path fires now.
description: Both are latent given current content (every example/exercise/note in all five books carries an id), but the stated goal is onboarding 3-4 new books whose authoring conventions are unknown; OpenStax CNXML does not require ids on these elements. If a new book ships id-less exercises, they vanish silently; id-less examples/notes render but lose figure dedup and SVG image localization.
recommendation: Make buildExerciseDom fall back to buildGenericElement like the other two. Add ctx as a parameter to buildGenericElement and thread it through its buildElement recursion. Cheap and removes a silent-loss footgun before unknown books arrive.

title: ~500 lines of legacy string-based builders retained and exported but dead in the dispatcher
evidence: The dispatcher buildElement:1731-1735 routes example/exercise/note exclusively to the *Dom variants. The original string builders buildExample:2146, buildExercise:2454, buildNote:2673 -- plus the string-path helpers they alone reach: replaceListItems:2016, listContainsReplacedParas:1995, replaceParaPreservingNested:2072, stripNestedElements:3040 -- are unreachable in production yet still exported (:3459-3463, comment 'Exported for comparison testing'). buildNote still contains its own divergent figure-caption and list logic.
description: This is parallel-implementation debt: two full rebuild engines for the same constructs. Fixes (e.g. the list-flattening unification above) can land in the wrong copy, and a reader cannot tell which path is live. It also doubles the regex surface a security/quality reviewer must audit.
recommendation: Delete the legacy buildExample/buildExercise/buildNote and their exclusively-reached string helpers, or move them into a test-only fixture module if the DOM-vs-regex comparison tests are still wanted. Keep one engine (DOM) as the single source of truth before onboarding more books.

title: isApiTranslated is a fragile marker-shape guess, not a real provenance signal — biology/microbiology will be systematically misrouted
evidence: cnxml-inject.js:3307-3313 decides the entire restore code path by sniffing whether any segment contains {{i}}/{{b}}/{{term}}/{{fn}}. But there are now two LIVE producers of 02-mt-output — api-translate.js:649 and docx-import.js:795 — while the only web-UI MT producers are archived (tools/archived/join-mt-output.js, prepare-for-align.js, translate-markdown.js). Measured in efnafraedi-2e: of 170 module files, 124 detected as API, 13 detected NON-API despite carrying bracket markers ([[i:]]/[[sub:]]/[[sup:]]), and 31 carry no inline markers at all. Extraction emits 0 **bold** and 0 __term__ source markers (110 files use {{term}}, only 11 use [[b:]]), so a module whose only inline markup is bracket emphasis/sub/sup and which has no term/footnote is API-translated yet detected as non-API. Biology and microbiology lack <example> and (microbiology) <glossary>, so far fewer {{term}}/{{fn}} markers — meaning a large fraction of those books' API output will be misclassified as non-API and pushed through the legacy/docx repair path.
description: The single gate that selects fragile-vs-robust handling is derived from incidental marker shapes rather than knowing who produced the file. It happens to work for chemistry (term/footnote-rich) but is structurally biased against the exact two books slated for onboarding next.
recommendation: Have api-translate.js and docx-import.js each stamp explicit producer provenance into 02-mt-output (a sidecar like the existing import-report.json, or a header comment) and gate on that instead of marker sniffing. This single change dissolves findings 2, 3 and 6's routing risk. Reuse the existing import-report.json convention docx-import already writes.

title: restoreNewlines / restoreMediaMarkers / restoreSupersubMarkers are near-dead for API content but live for docx-import — the gate mismatches both populations
evidence: These three run only when !isApiTranslated (cnxml-inject.js:3329-3351). Per-segment EN-vs-MT loss measured across all five books (scratchpad loss.mjs): efnafraedi-2e lost 0 [[BR]] and 0 [[MEDIA]]; edlisfraedi-2e, orverufraedi, lifraen-efnafraedi all 0. The only real MEDIA loss is liffraedi-2e (3 segments: m66440/m66442/m66443), and those modules are exactly the ones detected NON-API and were docx-imported (books/liffraedi-2e/02-mt-output/ch03/import-report.json). So api-translate output (hardened by normalizeSegMarkers, api-translate.js:290) essentially never loses these markers, while docx-import — which fuzzy-matches human prose blocks to segment IDs (docx-import.js:561-578) — does. The functions therefore earn their keep only on docx-imported content, yet their comments (cnxml-inject.js:399-403, 477-483) describe a retired 'web UI MT service'.
description: The repair scaffold is justified by a pipeline that no longer exists; its real beneficiary (docx-import) is undocumented, and the gate keys off a proxy that lines up with neither cleanly.

For API content they can be dropped or demoted to a warn-only loss check (compare EN/IS marker counts, log, do not mutate) — the durable fix is producer-side (normalizeSegMarkers/assertNoControlChars), not downstream reconstruction.

title: restoreMediaMarkers blindly appends [[MEDIA:N]] to the end of the IS text with no alignment check
evidence: cnxml-inject.js:513-531: when IS has zero media markers, it collects all [[BR]]/[[MEDIA:N]] from EN and does `isSegments.set(segId, result + markerStr)` — concatenating to the trimmed end of whatever IS text exists. For the live liffraedi-2e cases the docx-matched IS text is unrelated to the EN segment (e.g. m66443 EN begins '[[MEDIA:1]] In a double stranded DNA molecule…' while the matched IS is 'Ef stökkbreyting verður og adenín basa er skipt út fyrir sýtósín…'), so the figure marker is appended onto mismatched prose and ends up at the wrong position. In EN the marker is segment-initial, not terminal (line 527 comment even acknowledges 'text:[[BR]][[MEDIA:1]]' ordering is assumed).
description: Even where the repair fires legitimately (docx imports), placement is unreliable: it cannot reconstruct mid-segment or leading marker positions and silently puts them at the tail.
recommendation: When the EN marker is not segment-terminal, prefer anchor-based insertion (as restoreNewlines attempts at cnxml-inject.js:449-457) or skip with a warning rather than blind-append; gate the whole function behind docx provenance so it never touches clean API output.

title: restoreMathMarkers is the one genuinely-live fragile heuristic — ~190 lines of anchor/position tracking for 3 fixes book-wide
evidence: Unlike the others it runs for BOTH pipelines (cnxml-inject.js:3354) and spans restoreMathMarkers (558-641) plus restoreMathBySeparators (654-747). Strategy 2 builds an anchor from the last 15 chars of a 30-char window before the marker (605-609) and re-finds it via result.indexOf (613), then guesses an insertion span bounded by the next [[MATH:]]/label (616-621) — classic position-tracking that the audit context flags as the root of past render bugs. Measured live value is tiny: MATH loss is 3 segments in efnafraedi-2e and 0 in all four other books (loss.mjs). Failure mode: the short substring anchor matches an earlier identical fragment in the IS sentence and splices [[MATH:N]] into the wrong clause; the length<40 guard (624) limits but does not prevent mislocation.
description: High structural risk and high complexity for very low yield. It is the function most likely to silently corrupt a segment, and it is the only fragile one not shielded by the API gate.
recommendation: Move detection upstream: api-translate.js already has retry/backoff and assertNoControlChars; add a per-segment [[MATH:N]] count check there and re-translate the offending segment (or flag it) instead of reconstructing positions downstream. Keep the separator-based path (restoreMathBySeparators, which safely returns null on structural mismatch, 661-668) as a conservative fallback and retire the anchor path.

title: annotateInlineTerms attaches English glosses by ordinal position and desyncs on term reorder or count mismatch — wrong gloss reaches readers

In efnafraedi-2e (scratchpad terms.mjs over 21,441 aligned segments) 163 segments carry >=2 EN {{term}} markers (reorder risk — Icelandic word order differs) and 46 segments have EN {{term}} count != IS count (guaranteed positional desync; restoreTermMarkers does NOT trim excess {{term}}, only __ artifacts, so the mismatch survives to here). Coupling failure mode: annotateInlineTerms runs LAST in the mutation sequence (after restoreTermMarkers/MathMarkers), so any {{term}} or __ artifact those steps fail to normalise shifts every subsequent index, attaching the wrong gloss to every later term in the segment.
description: A reader-facing correctness bug, not just a fidelity nit: the wrong English term can be printed next to an Icelandic term. The blast radius is bounded (≈209 segments in chem) but grows per book and is invisible without spot checks.
recommendation: Skip annotation for any segment where EN and IS {{term}} counts differ (cheap, kills the 46 guaranteed-wrong cases), and prefer matching by content — cross-check the IS term text against the glossary's known translation of the EN term — over ordinal position. The glossary is already loaded for the API stage and could be reused here.

title: restoreGlossaryTermMarkup uses first-occurrence replace and appends MathML unconditionally — mis-wraps repeated short tokens

description: Every PhET simulation / YouTube concept-trailer embed in physics and biology is silently lost at extraction because the media handler is image-only. ~108 interactive assets disappear from the translated CNXML.
recommendation: In the media handlers, detect a child `<iframe>` (and other non-image media children) and record `{embedSrc, width, height}` in inlineMedia/structure so inject can reproduce it. Reuse parseAttributes. Rendering of the embed lives in namsbokasafn-vefur content.css/markup (FLAG: cross-repo).

title: Whitelist reconstruction model drops any unrecognized construct silently, with no diagnostic
evidence: extractInlineText ends with `stripTags(text)` (cnxml-extract.js:374) which deletes any inline element it did not explicitly convert. structure.json records only a fixed set of block types, and buildManifest counts a hardcoded whitelist (:1653-1665: para/section/figure/table/example/exercise/note/equation/list/media/glossary). inject (buildCnxml, cnxml-inject.js:1452) rebuilds output purely from structure.json. No warning is emitted for residual markup. A .cnxml-scoped tag inventory surfaces unhandled tags beyond the os-embed/iframe cases above: `<span>` 1074 (organic colored text), `<label>` 2223, `<colspec>` 1701, `<tgroup>` 555, `<thead>` 446 (table column/alignment/header structure not captured by processTable, which only reads row/entry, :1067-1108).
description: The pipeline is fail-open by omission: whatever extraction does not recognize is gone, with no log, count, or manifest flag. This is the root cause behind the os-embed, iframe, colored-span and table-internals losses, and the chief risk when onboarding any book with constructs chem lacks. A new book can lose content with zero signal.
recommendation: Add an unrecognized-element detector: before the final stripTags, scan for residual `<tag` tokens, accumulate per-tag counts, and surface them in the manifest (and a stderr warning in --verbose). This turns silent loss into a reviewable onboarding checklist. Also extend processTable to retain colspec/tgroup column metadata and thead/tbody designation.

title: `<term>` and `<footnote>` still emitted as legacy `{{ }}` markers — the lossy delimiter family, on the highest-volume inline elements
evidence: Terms become `{{term}}...{{/term}}` (cnxml-extract.js:303) and footnotes `{{fn}}...{{/fn}}` (:370), while sub/sup/emphasis/links were migrated to the ~0%-loss `[[ ]]` brackets (:246-359). Per CLAUDE.md / api-marker-survival, the `{{ }}` class measured ~97.7% survival (Erlendur `{{SEG}}`-stripping) vs ~100% for brackets. These are the largest-volume inline elements: .cnxml-scoped counts are 15,282 `<term>` + 578 `<footnote>` (liffraedi 4,799 terms; orverufraedi 6,395 terms + 458 footnotes). Same gap applies to `++underline++` (56 occurrences, :275, no bracket variant) and the untested `{=...=}` class-emphasis marker (30 occurrences, :281-289).
description: The marker migration that fixed loss for other inline elements skipped exactly the two highest-frequency ones. Even sub-1% loss across ~16k terms means hundreds of silently de-tagged terms per book (lost glossary links / term highlighting). Marker dialects also proliferate ([[ ]], {{ }}, {= =}, ++) with three of the four untested or known-lossy.
recommendation: Add bracket variants `[[term:...]]` / `[[fn:...]]` (and `[[u:...]]` for underline) in extractInlineText; injection is already backward-compatible per CLAUDE.md so old output keeps working. Consolidate the marker family on `[[ ]]` to retire the lossy/untested delimiters before scaling to books with thousands of terms/footnotes.

title: Document/module title containing inline markup extracts as "Untitled"
evidence: extractDocumentTitle (cnxml-parser.js:50-54) matches `<document...>[\s\S]*?<title>([^<]+)</title>`; the `[^<]+` cannot match a title that starts with or contains markup, and the lazy prefix then skips to a wrong/later title or fails. 32 module titles contain inline markup, almost all in lifraen-efnafraedi (e.g. `<emphasis effect="italics">sp</emphasis><sup>3</sup> Hybrid Orbitals...`, `p<emphasis>K</emphasis><sub>a</sub>`, `E,Z` stereochemistry). Verified: extractDocumentTitle on the sp³ module returns `"Untitled"`. The doc title also bypasses extractInlineText entirely (cnxml-extract.js:446 passes raw doc.title), unlike section/note/example titles which use it.
description: Module page titles with chemical/mathematical markup (heavily used in organic chemistry) are lost and replaced with 'Untitled'. 32 modules affected, concentrated in the next likely onboarding candidate.
recommendation: Change extractDocumentTitle to capture the full title inner content (`([\s\S]*?)`) and route it through extractInlineText (as section titles already are at cnxml-extract.js:653), so sub/sup/emphasis become markers instead of breaking the match.

title: Organic colored-text `<span class="*-text">` semantics flattened at extraction
evidence: 1074 `<span>` in organic .cnxml (184 files), all color classes: `magenta-text` 379, `red-text` 364, `cyan-text` 230, `green-text` 93, plus yellow/gray/purple. extractInlineText has no `<span>` case, so these reach the final `stripTags` (cnxml-extract.js:374): the text survives but the color class is dropped. In organic-chemistry reaction mechanisms these colors mark specific atoms/bonds/electron movement, so the chemistry-pedagogical signal is lost. (Confirmed unrelated: biology species italics use `<emphasis effect="italics">`, not `<foreign>` — 0 `<foreign>` in liffraedi .cnxml — so binomials ARE handled as `[[i:]]`.)
description: Color-coded text used pervasively in organic mechanisms is silently de-styled at extraction. Not text loss, but loss of meaning-bearing presentation specific to the organic book.
recommendation: Add a `<span class=...>` producer mirroring the existing class-emphasis sidecar pattern (cnxml-extract.js:281-289 `{=...=}` + collectedEmphasisAttrs) — e.g. `[[span:class|text]]` with the class stored in the inline-attrs sidecar so inject can restore it. Rendering of the color class lives in namsbokasafn-vefur content.css (FLAG: cross-repo).

title: No non-chemistry book is exercised end-to-end; the only integration test is efnafraedi-2e ch01
evidence: tools/__tests__/pipeline-integration.test.js:35-38 copies only books/efnafraedi-2e and runs inject+render against ch01 modules m68663/m68664 (106 it() blocks, all chemistry). The other four books appear in tool tests ONLY at config-unit granularity: liffraedi-2e/orverufraedi just exercise getBookRenderConfig/getExerciseSectionClasses/bookToDomain (cnxml-render.test.js:515-593, api-translate.test.js:189-193), and lifraen-efnafraedi appears once as a buildCnxml regression note (cnxml-inject.test.js:778). grep for 'iframe|os-embed' across tools/__tests__/ returns zero hits. Nothing currently proves that organic/physics/biology/microbiology source even renders to non-empty HTML.

Onboarding a 6th/7th book today would be flying blind: there is no signal that the new book's signature constructs survive the pipeline.
recommendation: Add one render-characterization spec per book using the existing inline-CNXML-string pattern already at cnxml-render.test.js:204-235 (feed a synthetic <document> straight to renderCnxmlToHtml — no MT input or full inject run needed, so it does not depend on whether 02-mt-output exists for non-chem books). Each fixture should embed that book's signature construct: organic <link class="os-embed"> exercise + <section class="key-terms">; physics/biology <iframe> embed; microbiology footnote + each of its 7 note classes. Assert the construct produces non-empty, expected HTML. Do the next-to-onboard book first.
