title: cnxml-parser.js — the string/regex core of the entire render path — has zero direct unit tests
evidence: No file under tools/__tests__/ imports '../lib/cnxml-parser' (grep -rl returns nothing). cnxml-parser.js is 374 lines / 13 exported functions including the two linchpin extractors: extractElements (naive non-greedy regex, line 186-204, used 16× by render) and extractNestedElements (manual depth counter, line 228-, used 32× by render). They are exercised only indirectly through render's higher-level tests, so their edge cases are unspecified.
description: extractNestedElements is the function that makes ALL structural nesting work in render (example/exercise/note/section/list/figure/media). Its depth counter at parser.js:242 does content.indexOf('<media', idx) / '<list', idx — an untested edge: a self-closing same-tag element (e.g. <media .../>) is counted as an opening tag with no matching close, which would mis-pair depth. Media-in-media and self-closing lists don't occur in practice today, so this is an untested edge, not a confirmed live bug — but it is exactly the kind of latent fault a refactor would trip over with no test to catch it.
recommendation: Add tools/__tests__/cnxml-parser.test.js covering extractElements (paired, self-closing, attribute parsing, sibling repetition) and extractNestedElements (same-tag nesting at depth 2-3, self-closing same-tag sibling, malformed/unterminated input, mixed self-closing + paired). This pins the contract before any render refactor touches it.
recommendation_note: gates the wanted render refactor, not the next book onboarding.

title: Render structural-nesting coverage is two narrow regressions; the figure/list/media-in-container × xref matrix is almost empty
evidence: cnxml-render.test.js has 56 it() blocks but only 2 structural-nesting cases: standalone <media> in a note (line 199) and a direct-child example <figure> cross-referenced by its intro para (line 218). grep for 'nested|<list|sublist' in the render test returns zero. There is no render test for: nested <list> (renderList recurses at cnxml-render.js:1887), figure/list/media inside an <exercise> (renderExercise structural extraction at 1602/1643-1654), table inside note/example, or nested <section> (renderSection recurses at 904). The xref-vs-no-xref dimension has exactly one cell filled (line 218, xref present).
description: These are precisely the shapes that produced all three historical render bugs (figure-escapes-example, dropped <media> in notes, duplicate figures) — and the lens's structural-nesting concern. Render reimplements this extraction via regex/strip-and-re-extract, independent of inject, so the bugs recur in render specifically. Without a coverage matrix, a render refactor cannot tell whether it preserved these behaviors.
recommendation: Build a small render nesting matrix using the inline-CNXML pattern at lines 204-235: {figure, list, media, table} × {example, exercise, note, section} × {with xref to it, without}, asserting the child renders exactly once and inside its parent container (reuse the figIdx < exampleCloseIdx ordering assertion from line 237-241). Start with the four shapes behind the historical bugs.
recommendation_note: gates the render refactor; partially relevant to onboarding books with heavy nesting.

title: Coverage asymmetry: inject DOM builders are nesting-tested; render's parallel string-based builders share none of it
evidence: Inject's structural builders have dedicated nesting suites: cnxml-inject.test.js 'buildExampleDom nested list in para' (700), 'buildExampleDom figure inside para' (777), 'buildExerciseDom figure inside para' (923), plus cnxml-dom.test.js (40 it() on replaceParaContent/replaceListItems/removeElementsByTag) and cnxml-dom-comparison.test.js (4 old-vs-new buildExample diffs). Render's renderExample (cnxml-render.js:1354), renderExercise (1602), renderNote (1255) reimplement the same child-extraction via extractElements/extractNestedElements with NO equivalent suite — e.g. inject tests figure-in-exercise (923) but render has no figure-in-exercise test at all.
description: The inject side uses a real DOM (@xmldom/xmldom via cnxml-dom.js) and is the better-tested half; render uses regex string-parsing and is the historically buggier, less-tested half. The test investment is inverted relative to the risk. A reviewer trusting 'inject nesting is covered' may wrongly assume render is too.
recommendation: Mirror the three inject buildXxxDom nesting describe blocks (inject.test.js:700/777/923) as render specs against renderExample/renderExercise/renderNote, reusing the same fixtures. Where feasible, share fixture CNXML between the inject and render specs so the two halves are tested on identical inputs.

title: Documented cross-book gaps (os-embed exercises, iframe embeds) have no characterization test — including the os-embed path that DOES exist
evidence: CORRECTION to brief: organic exercises do NOT simply 'render empty' — render has an os-embed resolution path (cnxml-render.js:134 cache lookup, :1704 'Check for os-embed exercise reference', :1745 fallback). But grep 'os-embed' in tools/__tests__/ = zero hits, so whether it resolves ~1961 organic exercises or falls through to the :1745 fallback is UNVERIFIED. Separately, <iframe> has no handling in either tool (grep 'iframe' in cnxml-render.js and cnxml-inject.js = zero) and no test — confirming physics/biology PhET/YouTube embeds (~57/51) are silently dropped with no test pinning that behavior.
description: These are the highest-volume cross-book constructs and the most likely to ship broken for the next non-chem book. With no characterization test asserting current behavior (resolved vs empty vs dropped), there is neither a TDD anchor for the fix nor a regression guard for a refactor. The os-embed case is especially sharp: code exists but its real-content behavior is unproven.
recommendation: Add characterization tests that assert today's actual behavior: (a) an os-embed exercise fixture through renderCnxmlToHtml asserting resolved-vs-fallback output (this also documents whether the ~1961 organic exercises work); (b) an <iframe> fixture asserting the current drop (a failing/xfail test documenting the gap, to flip when handling lands). Use the inline-CNXML pattern from line 204.
recommendation_note: the os-embed verification blocks onboarding organic specifically.

title: Render correctness depends on untested strip-before-extract ordering — the duplicate-figure bug class has no ordering guard
evidence: renderSection/renderExample/renderExercise extract children from progressively stripped copies of the content (cnxml-render.js:741 contentWithoutSections, 968 contentForSimpleElements, 1289 contentForParas, 1480 directFigures from contentForSimpleElements, 1653 contentWithoutFigures). extractElements (naive regex, parser.js:186) is safe for para/equation only because nested containers are stripped out first by these steps. No unit test pins this strip ordering: the duplicate-figure regression (pipeline-integration.test.js:272) and figure-escapes-example (render.test.js:218) are tested only as their specific symptom, not as the ordering invariant.
description: All three historical render bugs are strip-ordering faults: a child container left in the string before a naive para/figure extract gets emitted twice or escapes its parent. A refactor that reorders or consolidates these strip steps would silently reintroduce that bug class, and the current symptom-specific tests would not necessarily catch a new manifestation. (Note: extractElements for para/equation is itself fine — para/equation don't nest in CNXML — so the risk is the ordering, not the regex.)
recommendation: Add a render differential/snapshot harness modeled on cnxml-dom-comparison.test.js (4 old-vs-new diffs) plus compareTagCounts from cnxml-fidelity-check.js: snapshot renderCnxmlToHtml output (and per-tag counts) across a chemistry corpus sample, so any refactor must prove byte/tag-count identity. This is the concrete 'safe to refactor render' guard and reuses existing utilities.

title: Of ~609 tool tests, only 4 perform old-vs-new differential comparison and all 4 are inject-only
evidence: Total it()/test() across tools/__tests__/*.js = 609. cnxml-dom-comparison.test.js (the only differential suite, importing compareTagCounts from cnxml-fidelity-check.js and diffing buildExampleOld vs buildExampleDom) has 4 it() and imports '../cnxml-inject.js' only — render is never differentially compared. Per-file pipeline counts: render 56, inject 70, dom 40, dom-comparison 4, integration 106, extract 40.
description: The project already owns the right refactor-safety primitive (compareTagCounts + old-vs-new structure) but applies it only to inject's DOM migration. The render rewrite the scale goal calls for has no equivalent net, which is why every render change to date has shipped on hand-built symptom tests.
recommendation: Extend the dom-comparison approach to render before refactoring: a corpus-level render snapshot/tag-count baseline that the refactor must match. Generalize compareTagCounts usage so the same utility guards both halves of the pipeline.

title: Document order is re-derived by string search (63 indexOf sites, 5 near-duplicate positioner blocks) instead of read from the parse — the root fragility class
evidence: tools/cnxml-render.js: 63 `.indexOf(` calls total (31 of form indexOf(`id="…"`), 28 of form indexOf(item.fullMatch), 7 bare-tag fallbacks). The same 'extract elements → strip containers with String.replace(fullMatch,'') → recompute each element's position with content.indexOf → sort by position' pattern is copy-pasted across five blocks: top-level loop (lines 718-834), renderTopLevelContent (924-1101), renderNote body (1280-1327), renderExample body (1409-1525), and renderSectionContent inside renderExercise (1643-1696). cnxml-parser.js already exports a single ordered-pass walker walkContent (line 351) that the render path never uses; the inject path (cnxml-dom.js, @xmldom) reads order from a real DOM. efnafraedi-2e (only rendered book) scores 0 on every collision metric below — nothing breaks today; all risk is latent and surfaces as the other four books onboard.
description: Order information already exists in the source byte stream and in extraction order, but every renderer throws it away and reconstructs it by searching the string for each element again. indexOf always returns the FIRST match, so any non-uniqueness (duplicate serialization, substring overlap, id-less elements, self-closing tags) silently produces wrong positions, ties, or -1→0. This is the architectural asymmetry the task names: render parses by regex/indexOf while inject trusts a DOM. The three historical render bugs (figure-escapes-example, dropped media, duplicate figures) are all instances of this class.
recommendation: Converge the five positioner blocks onto ONE ordered single-pass emitter rather than patching each indexOf. Two reuse paths already in-repo: (a) walkContent (cnxml-parser.js:351) — verify its regex handles your nesting (notes/examples/figures-in-paras) before drop-in; (b) preferred: route render through @xmldom like cnxml-inject.js/cnxml-dom.js already do, walking childNodes in native document order so position is never recomputed. Do this now while efnafraedi-2e is the only mature book and regressions are cheap to detect.

title: id-less <para> inside <note> renders out of order — deterministic for 95 notes across 77 biology modules
evidence: renderNote positions paras at tools/cnxml-render.js:1290-1294: `const pos = para.id ? contentWithoutTitle.indexOf(`id="${para.id}"`) : contentWithoutTitle.indexOf('<para')`. liffraedi-2e/01-source has 95 paras with no id, ALL inside <note> (verified: inExercise=0, inNote=95), in 77 modules. Every one follows the pattern [<para id=…>, <para NO-ID>] (e.g. m66430.cnxml, m66436.cnxml). The id-less second para resolves to indexOf('<para') = the FIRST para's opening-tag offset, which is a few chars LESS than the first para's indexOf('id=…'); the sort therefore emits the id-less para BEFORE the id-bearing one, inverting document order. The exercise variant is worse: renderSectionContent line 1658 uses `sectionContent.indexOf(`id="${para.id}"`)` with no bare fallback, so an id-less para yields indexOf('id="null"') → -1 → position 0 (silently pinned to top).
description: Unlike the other books, OpenStax biology emits paragraphs without ids (95; edlisfraedi 1; chem/organic/micro 0). The id-less fallback collapses them to the first-para offset (or to 0 in exercises), so any note that mixes id-bearing and id-less paras renders them in the wrong order. Confirmed deterministic from structure for biology; will manifest the moment liffraedi-2e is onboarded.
recommendation: Fixed for free by the F1 ordered-pass/DOM convergence. If patching in place first, position id-less paras by their actual match offset (use the para's fullMatch from extractElements, which is populated, instead of the id/bare-tag search) and never emit indexOf('id="null"') for a null id (guard the null at lines 1658, 1668).
blocks_next_book_note: if biology (liffraedi-2e) is the next onboard

title: Positioning by indexOf(`id="X"`) substring-collides with target-id="X"/document target-id references — the already-fixed bug class, still live in the positioners
evidence: The needle `id="X"` is a substring of `target-id="X"`, `document="…" target-id="X"`, and `reference="X"`. So content.indexOf(`id="X"`) can return an earlier xref instead of the element's own open tag. This exact trap was fixed for the figure isInsidePara check — see the comment at tools/cnxml-render.js:1483-1486 ('Match the figure's own opening tag … NOT a bare id="X" substring … the latter also matches a sibling para's <link target-id="X"/>'). But 31 positioner sites still use the bare substring: para at 829/1092/1293/1436, figure at 1300/1668, list at 1320/1672, plus ~16 dead id-fallback ternaries. String-scan counts of `id="X"` whose first occurrence sits inside a target-id: efnafraedi 701/108 mod, edlisfraedi 1263/238, liffraedi 1118/207, organic 650/251, micro 1019/128. Two reach a real <para> (organic m00016 para-00014; micro m58810 fs-id1168328231014) — but BOTH escape misorder: m00016's para is inside a <table> cell (rendered via renderTable, net section depth aside), and m58810's xref is one section level deeper than its target (between offsets: 4 <section> opens vs 5 closes → different scope), and the positioners run on section-scoped content. So currently latent: only section-scoping accidentally saves it.
description: The positioners trust a whole-string id search that is not anchored to an element open tag, exactly the pattern already recognized as a bug elsewhere in the same file. The two concrete hits today are neutralized by table-cell routing and cross-section scope, not by any guard — a forward xref to a LATER <para>/<figure>/<list> within the SAME section would silently misorder it. The precondition is widespread (650-1263 substrings/book).
recommendation: Anchor the search to the element's own open tag (`<para … id="X"` / reuse the figure pattern at 1488) or, better, eliminate id-based position lookup entirely via the F1 ordered pass. Do not rely on the empirical 'only 2 hits' — that count is whole-module; same-section forward references are the unguarded case.
severity_note: precondition present (string scan); no rendered misorder confirmed — both detected cases escape via scope/table routing

title: Guarding is inconsistent across the five copied positioner blocks — containers are fullMatch-guarded in the main loops but id-positioned in renderNote/renderExercise
evidence: Main loop (tools/cnxml-render.js:771-826) and renderTopLevelContent (983-1088) position figure/note/example/exercise/table/media/list by content.indexOf(item.fullMatch) (unique full serialization → safe). But the copies drifted: renderNote positions figure by id (1299-1301) and list by id (1320-1322); renderSectionContent (exercise) positions para by id (1658), figure by id (1668), list by id (1672) — only media keeps the fullMatch guard (1313, 1662). So the same element type is collision-safe in one block and exposed in another, with no test pinning the divergence. The id="null" pos-0 pile (F2) is a direct consequence at 1658/1668.
description: Five hand-maintained copies of one algorithm have diverged in exactly the dimension that matters (which key is used to recover position). A reader cannot tell from one block whether a given element type is guarded; fixes applied to one block (e.g. the 1483-1486 figure fix) were not propagated to the others. This is the maintenance hazard that makes the whole class hard to reason about as more books add element shapes.
recommendation: Collapse to a single positioning helper (ideally the F1 DOM/walkContent pass). If kept as-is short-term, make every block position by fullMatch (already populated by extractNestedElements/extractElements for all of figure/note/example/exercise/table/media/list/equation/para) and delete the id/bare-tag fallbacks, so all five blocks share one safe key.

title: id-less ordering correctness silently depends on V8 stable sort, and container-strip uses String.replace (first-occurrence only) with no duplicate guard
evidence: When multiple elements tie on position (id-less paras at indexOf('<para'), or the pos-0/-1→0 cases), correct relative order relies entirely on Array.prototype.sort being stable (true in Node 22, but never asserted or tested). Separately, container stripping uses `simpleContent = simpleContent.replace(e.fullMatch, '')` (tools/cnxml-render.js:752-766, 941-978, 1287, 1310, 1648) — String.replace with a string argument removes only the FIRST occurrence. If two elements ever share byte-identical serialization, the second strip is a no-op (residue leaks into para/media extraction) and indexOf(fullMatch) pins both to the same offset. Measured duplicate-fullMatch elements in source: 0 across all 5 books (figure/note/example/exercise/table/media/list/para/equation), so this is theoretical today.
description: Two latent assumptions underpin ordering: stable sort, and globally-unique element serialization. Both hold on current source but neither is enforced. Machine translation can synthesize identical short paragraphs/media captions across a module, at which point the strip becomes lossy/duplicating — the same shape as the historical duplicate-figure render bug (though that one's root cause was nesting-strip leakage, not replace()).
recommendation: When the F1 ordered pass lands, both concerns vanish (no strip, no resort). Until then: add a one-line comment/test pinning stable-sort reliance, and prefer offset-based splicing over replace(fullMatch,'') so identical serializations can't collide. Do not treat the 0-in-source count as permanent — it is an input property, not a guarantee.

title: Depth counter in extractNestedElements/removeNestedElements has no word boundary and no self-closing-tag branch
evidence: cnxml-parser.js:242-243 and cnxml-render.js:2058-2059 advance depth with content.indexOf(`<${tagName}`, idx) / indexOf(`</${tagName}>`). The open-tag probe `<tagName` has no trailing boundary, so for a tagName that prefixes another element it would over-count (CNXML has no such sibling for the tags used, so safe today). More material: a self-closing `<media .../>` (or any `<tag/>`) increments depth via the `<tag` probe but is never matched by a `</tag>`, so depth can never return to 0 for the intended element — the scan runs to the next unrelated close tag or EOF, returning an over-long fullMatch. Standalone self-closed media is exactly a cross-book shape (notes/figures with single <media/> children). Also ~16 id-fallback ternary branches (e.g. lines 772,803,817,986,1027,1060,1082,1315,1410,1457,1499,1520,1664) are currently unreachable (extract* always sets fullMatch) but encode the unsafe substring pattern as latent traps.
description: The manual brace-matching that underlies every extractNestedElements/removeNestedElements call assumes paired open/close tags and exact name matches. Self-closing same-name tags and name-prefix overlaps both break the depth invariant. No book currently triggers it, but it is the kind of shape a newly-onboarded book introduces (the task already flags self-contained media and varied element forms).
recommendation: Add a self-closing branch (treat `<tag …/>` as depth-neutral) and a word-boundary to the open probe (`<tag` followed by whitespace, `>`, or `/`). Or, again, retire both functions in favor of the @xmldom traversal inject already uses. Delete the dead id-fallback ternaries so the unsafe pattern stops being copied.

title: CSS-contract test is scoped to efnafraedi-2e only and skips silently when vefur is absent — the keystone gap for onboarding new books
evidence: tools/__tests__/css-contract.test.js:20 hardcodes PUBLICATION_DIR to books/efnafraedi-2e/05-publication; lines 102/162/198 use it.skipIf(!vefurExists || !pubExists) — when ../../../namsbokasafn-vefur is not checked out (CI per MEMORY: 'credits exhausted, local-gate only'), the entire contract suite is a no-op with a green tick. The 'dead selectors' check (line 162) only console.logs, never fails. Cross-book classes (note-microbiology, clinical-focus, biology multi-type exercises) are never scanned.
description: This single test is the only automated link between render output (efni) and content.css (vefur). It validates exactly one book and degrades to a silent pass in the very environment (CI without the sister repo) where regressions would otherwise be caught. As books 2-5 onboard, their render classes will go entirely unverified against vefur, so the class/structure mismatches the rest of these findings describe will land in production HTML undetected. It is the generator of unknown-unknowns for the scale goal.
recommendation: Parametrize the test over every book that has a 05-publication tree (glob books/*/05-publication), not just efnafraedi-2e. Convert the vefur-absent path from skipIf to a hard fail when an env flag (e.g. VEFUR_CONTRACT=1) is set, so the local gate and any future CI must have vefur present; keep skip only for ad-hoc dev. title: Note rendering passes raw CNXML class attributes straight into HTML class names, coupling every new book's note vocabulary to vefur content.css
